claim: Thoracic tracheoblasts are arrested in the G2 phase of the cell cycle in an ATR (mei-41)-Checkpoint Kinase1 (grapes, Chk1) dependent manner prior to mitotic re-entry.
source: Thoracic tracheoblasts are arrested in the G2 phase of the cell cycle in an ATR (mei-41)-Checkpoint Kinase1 (grapes, Chk1) dependent manner prior to mitotic re-entry.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing that loss of Chk1 leads to precocious proliferation.

claim: Wnt signaling is high in tracheoblasts and this is necessary for high levels of activated (phosphorylated) Chk1.
source: We report that Wnt signaling is high in tracheoblasts and this is necessary for high levels of activated (phosphorylated) Chk1.
evidence: Supported by reporter expression data (Fz3-GFP, Nkd-LacZ) and pChk1 immunostaining in Wnt pathway mutants.

claim: Canonical Wnt signaling facilitates high levels of phosphorylated Chk1 by transcriptional upregulation of Chk1 expression in cells that have ATR kinase activity.
source: We find that canonical Wnt signaling facilitates this by transcriptional upregulation of Chk1 expression in cells that have ATR kinase activity.
evidence: Supported by qPCR data showing Chk1 mRNA levels are reduced in TCF mutants and Chk1-lacZ reporter expression data.

claim: Wnt signaling is dependent on four Wnts (Wg, Wnt5, 6, 10) that are expressed at high levels in arrested tracheoblasts and are downregulated at mitotic re-entry.
source: Wnt signaling is dependent on four Wnts (Wg, Wnt5, 6,10) that are expressed at high levels in arrested tracheoblasts and are downregulated at mitotic re-entry.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and smFISH data showing temporal expression patterns of these Wnt ligands.

claim: None of the Wnts (Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6, Wnt10) are dispensable and act synergistically to induce Chk1.
source: Interestingly, none of the Wnts are dispensable and act synergistically to induce Chk1.
evidence: Supported by data showing that knockdown of any single Wnt ligand leads to reduced Chk1 expression and precocious proliferation.

claim: Downregulation of Wnt signaling and Chk1 expression leads to mitotic re-entry and the concomitant upregulation of Dpp signaling, driving tracheoblast proliferation.
source: Finally, we show that downregulation of Wnt signaling and Chk1 expression leads to mitotic re-entry and the concomitant upregulation of Dpp signaling, driving tracheoblast proliferation.
evidence: Supported by pMad immunostaining showing Dpp signaling is activated in Chk1 and Wnt pathway mutants at early L3.

claim: Tracheoblasts in the Dorsal Trunk (DT) in Tr2 enter larval life in G1, transition from G1 to S to G2 in the first larval instar (L1) and remain arrested in G2 from second instar (L2) till 32–40 hr into third larval instar (L3) whereupon they re-enter mitosis.
source: Tracheoblasts in the Dorsal Trunk (DT) in Tr2 enter larval life in G1, transition from G1 to S to G2 in the first larval instar (L1) and remain arrested in G2 from second instar (L2) till 32–40 hr into third larval instar (L3) whereupon they re-enter mitosis (Figure 1A; Kizhedathu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by FUCCI reporter data shown in Figure 1A and previous publication.

claim: Tracheoblasts express high levels of Chk1 mRNA and phosphorylated Chk1 (pChk1) during the period in which they are paused in G2 and downregulate levels of Chk1 mRNA and pChk1 upon mitotic re-entry.
source: These cells express high levels of Chk1 mRNA and phosphorylated Chk1 (pChk1) during the period in which they are paused in G2 and downregulate levels of Chk1 mRNA and pChk1 upon mitotic re-entry.
evidence: Supported by qPCR data for Chk1 mRNA and pChk1 immunostaining at different larval stages.

claim: Loss of Chk1 leads to precocious proliferation by 16–24 h L3, approximately 24 hr earlier than expected.
source: Loss of Chk1 leads to precocious proliferation by 16–24 h L3,~24 hr earlier than expected (Figure 1B, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by cell count data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Knockdown of Fz2, Dsh and TCF (Pangolin) did not affect numbers of tracheoblasts in L2 but led to increased numbers at 16–24 h L3.
source: Knockdown of Fz2, Dsh and TCF (Pangolin) did not affect numbers of tracheoblasts in L2 but led to increased numbers at 16–24 h L3 (Figure 1B,n ≥ 7 tracheae per timepoint here and in all subsequent figures showing cell frequencies, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by cell count data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Knockdown of Arm did not perturb numbers of cells in Tr2 DT in L2 but led to increased numbers of cells at 24 h L3.
source: Knockdown of Arm did not perturb numbers of cells in Tr2 DT in L2 but led to increased numbers of cells at 24 h L3 (Figure 1C,n ≥ 7 tracheae per condition, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by cell count data shown in Figure 1C using temperature-sensitive GAL80 system.

claim: Levels of expression of fz3-GFP and nkd-lacZ were high at L2 and 0–8 h L3 and significantly lower at 32–40 hr into L3.
source: Immunostaining using anti-GFP and anti-β-gal antisera respectively revealed that levels of expression of fz3-GFP and nkd-lacZ were high at L2 and 0–8 h L3 and significantly lower at 32–40 hr into L3 (Figure 1F, n = 6 tracheae per condition per experiment, n = 2).
evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The expression of Fz3 mRNA is high in L2 and early L3 and significantly lower at 32–40 h L3.
source: qPCR analysis showed that the expression of Fz3 mRNA is high in L2 and early L3 and significantly lower at 32–40 h L3 (Figure 1G, n = 3).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Canonical Wnt signaling is active in G2 arrested cells and is downregulated upon mitotic re-entry.
source: These data show that canonical Wnt signaling is active in G2 arrested cells and is downregulated upon mitotic re-entry.
evidence: Inferred from reporter expression and qPCR data showing high Wnt signaling during G2 arrest and low signaling at mitotic re-entry.

claim: The levels of pChk1 were dramatically reduced in Btl-TCFRNAi at L2 in comparison to wild type.
source: pChk1 immunostaining in Btl-TCFRNAi at L2 showed that the levels of pChk1 were dramatically reduced in comparison to wild type (Figure 2A, n = 6–8 tracheae per condition per experiment, n = 3).
evidence: Supported by pChk1 immunostaining data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The Wnt pathway is required for Chk1 activation in the tracheoblasts.
source: We inferred that the Wnt pathway is required Chk1 activation in the tracheoblasts.
evidence: Inferred from data showing reduced pChk1 levels in Wnt pathway mutants.

claim: Levels of pChk1 and Chk1 mRNA are correlated in Tr2 DT.
source: Our earlier studies have shown that levels of pChk1 and Chk1 mRNA are correlated in Tr2 DT.
evidence: Referenced from previous studies (Kizhedathu et al., 2018).

claim: Both pChk1 and Chk1 mRNA levels are high in L2 and early L3 and diminish at 32–40 h L3.
source: In other words, both pChk1 and Chk1 mRNA levels are high in L2 and early L3 and diminish at 32–40 h L3.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and immunostaining data from this study and previous work.

claim: Overexpression of Chk1 is sufficient to induce G2 arrest in yeast, Drosophila, and Xenopus.
source: Studies in yeast (Ford et al., 1994), Drosophila (Bayer et al., 2018) and Xenopus (Kumagai et al., 1998) have shown that the overexpression of Chk1 is sufficient to induce G2 arrest.
evidence: Cited from multiple published studies.

claim: The loss of Wnt signaling (Btl-TCFRNAi) led to a reduction in Chk1 levels at L2 and early L3; the levels of expression at these stages were comparable to 32–40 h L3.
source: The loss of Wnt signaling (Btl-TCFRNAi) led to a reduction in Chk1 levels at L2 and early L3; the levels of expression at these stages were comparable to 32–40 h L3.
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Overexpression of ArmS10 led to an increase in the level of Chk1 transcript.
source: Conversely, overexpression of ArmS10 led to an increase in the level of Chk1 transcript (Figure 3A,≥15 tracheal fragments per timepoint per experiment, n = 3 experiments).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: β-gal expression from Chk1-lacZ is high in L2 and early L3 and declines at 32–40 hr into L3.
source: Anti-β-gal immunostaining of tracheae from Chk1-lacZ animals at different larval stages showed that β-gal expression is high in L2 and early L3 and declines at 32–40 hr into L3 (Figure 3B, n = 6 tracheae per condition per experiment, n = 2).
evidence: Supported by β-gal immunostaining data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: β-gal expression from Chk1-lacZ was considerably diminished in Btl-TCFRNAi animals at L2.
source: We found that β-gal expression was considerably diminished in L2 (Figure 3B, n = 6 tracheae per condition per experiment, n = 2).
evidence: Supported by β-gal immunostaining data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Wnt signaling is required for high levels of Chk1 expression in G2-arrested cells.
source: Together, the analysis of Chk1 mRNA levels and Chk1-lacZ in control and Wnt signaling-deficient tracheoblasts show that Wnt signaling is required for high levels of Chk1 expression in G2-arrested cells.
evidence: Inferred from qPCR and reporter expression data.

claim: Chk1 overexpression prevented premature mitotic re-entry in Btl-TCFRNAi animals.
source: Cell counts in Tr2 DT at 16–24 h L3 in Wild type, Btl-TCFRNAi, Btl-TCFRNAi, Chk1 (TCF knockdown with Chk1 overexpression) and Btl-TCFRNAi, ATR (TCF knockdown with ATR overexpression) expressing animals showed that Chk1 overexpression did indeed prevent premature mitotic re-entry (Figure 3C, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by cell count data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: ATR overexpression did not prevent premature mitotic re-entry in Btl-TCFRNAi animals.
source: The overexpression of ATR did not (Figure 3C, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by cell count data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The levels of pChk1 were high and comparable to wild type in Btl-TCFRNAi, Chk1 animals.
source: Immunostaining for pChk1 revealed that the levels were high and comparable to wild type in Btl-TCFRNAi, Chk1 animals.
evidence: Supported by pChk1 immunostaining data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The levels of pChk1 were not restored in Btl-TCFRNAi, ATR expressing animals and were comparable to Btl-Chk1RNAi animals at the same stage.
source: In contrast, the levels of pChk1 were not restored in Btl-TCFRNAi, ATR expressing animals and were comparable to Btl-Chk1RNAi animals at the same stage (Figure 3D–E, n = 6 tracheae per experiment, n = 2).
evidence: Supported by pChk1 immunostaining data shown in Figures 3D-E.

claim: Wnt dependent regulation of Chk1 expression is necessary for G2 arrest in Tr2 DT.
source: These data support the hypothesis that Wnt dependent regulation of Chk1 expression is necessary for G2 arrest in Tr2 DT.
evidence: Inferred from rescue experiments showing Chk1 overexpression restores G2 arrest in TCF mutants.

claim: mRNA levels of 4 Wnt ligands – Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6 and Wnt10 - are high in L2 and 0–8 h L3 and low at 32–40 h L3.
source: The analysis revealed that mRNA levels of 4 Wnt ligands – Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6 and Wnt10 - are high in L2 and 0–8 h L3 and low at 32–40 h L3 (Figure 4A, ≥15 tracheal fragments per timepoint per experiment, n = 3 experiments).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Wnt2, Wnt4 and WntD were undetectable in the tracheae at all stages.
source: Wnt2, Wnt4 and WntD were undetectable in the tracheae at all stages (data not shown).
evidence: Stated as experimental observation from qPCR analysis.

claim: smFISH for Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6 and Wnt10 detected both nuclear spots and faint spots in the cytoplasm in virtually all the cells in Tr2 DT at L2.
source: smFISH for Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6 and Wnt10 detected both nuclear spots and faint spots in the cytoplasm in virtually all the cells in Tr2 DT at L2 (Figure 4B) and 0–8 h L3 (data not shown).
evidence: Supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Neither the prominent nuclear spots nor faint cytoplasmic signals for Wnt ligands were detectable at 32–40 h L3.
source: Neither the prominent nuclear spots (Figure 4B arrowheads) nor faint cytoplasmic signals were detectable at 32–40 h L3.
evidence: Supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Knockdown of Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6 and Wnt10 in the trachea led to an increase in cell number at 16–24 hr into L3.
source: Knockdown of Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6 and Wnt10 in the trachea led to an increase in cell number at 16–24 hr into L3 (Figure 4C, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by cell count data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: There was an increase in pH3+ figures in Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6 and Wnt10 knockdown backgrounds at 16–24 h L3.
source: There was also an increase in pH3+figures in these backgrounds at 16–24 h L3 (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by pH3 quantification data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There were increased numbers of cells in Wgts, Wnt5[400], and Wnt6 mutants at 16–24 h L3.
source: We found an increase in cell numbers in Wgts animals that were raised at 29°C (Figure 4E, Figure 4—source data 1). Cell counts at L2 and16-24 h L3 in Wnt5[400], Wnt6 mutants and Btl-Wnt10RNAi (btl-GAL4/UAS-Wnt10RNAi) showed that there were increased numbers of cells in these backgrounds at 16–24 h L3 (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: Supported by cell count data shown in Figure 4E and supplement.

claim: Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6 and Wnt10 are required to maintain G2 arrest in Tr2 DT.
source: Taken together, these data show that Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6 and Wnt10 are required to maintain G2 arrest in Tr2 DT.
evidence: Inferred from cell proliferation data in mutants for these ligands.

claim: The reduction of expression of any one Wnt ligand did not impact the expression of others.
source: We found that the reduction of expression of any one ligand did not impact the expression of others (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,≥15 tracheal fragments per timepoint per experiment, n = 3 experiments).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The expression of each of the Wnt ligands is independent of the others and each ligand contributes toward G2 arrest.
source: Based on this analysis, we inferred that the expression of each of the Wnt ligands is independent of the others and that each ligand contributes toward G2 arrest.
evidence: Inferred from qPCR data showing independent expression patterns.

claim: Levels of pChk1 in Btl-WgRNAi, Btl-Wnt5RNAi, Btl-Wnt6RNAi and Btl-Wnt10RNAi were diminished, comparable to what was observed in Btl-Chk1RNAi expressing animals.
source: pChk1 immunostaining of Btl-WgRNAi, Btl-Wnt5RNAi, Btl-Wnt6RNAi and Btl-Wnt10RNAi showed that levels of pChk1 in each of these backgrounds was diminished, the extent of the reduction in staining was comparable to what was observed in Btl-Chk1RNAi expressing animals (Figure 4F, compare with Figure 2A (ii)).
evidence: Supported by pChk1 immunostaining data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The loss of any one of the Wnt ligands (Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6, Wnt10) led to diminished levels of Chk1 mRNA expression comparable to the levels detected in Btl-TCFRNAi.
source: Quantification of Chk1 mRNA in Btl-TCFRNAi, Btl-WgRNAi, Btl-Wnt5RNAi, Btl-Wnt6RNAi and Btl-Wnt10RNAi showed that the loss of any one of the ligands led to diminished levels of Chk1 mRNA expression. The levels of mRNA in each of these mutant backgrounds was comparable to the levels detected in Btl-TCFRNAi (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: All four Wnt ligands (Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6, Wnt10) regulate Chk1 expression in Tr2 DT.
source: Together, these data showed that all four ligands regulate Chk1 expression in Tr2 DT.
evidence: Inferred from data showing each ligand knockdown reduces Chk1 expression.

claim: There was no significant change in Fz3 mRNA levels in Btl-WgRNAi, Btl-Wnt5RNAi, Btl-Wnt6RNAi and Btl-Wnt10RNAi.
source: There was no significant change in Fz3 mRNA levels in Btl-WgRNAi, Btl-Wnt5RNAi, Btl-Wnt6RNAi and Btl-Wnt10RNAi (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The levels of Fz3 were considerably reduced in Btl-TCFRNAi.
source: However, the levels of Fz3 were considerably reduced in Btl-TCFRNAi
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The expression of any one of the Wnt ligands is sufficient to induce Fz3 expression in Tr2 DT but all four are required to induce Chk1 expression.
source: We infer that the expression of any one of the abovementioned Wnt ligands is sufficient to induce Fz3 expression in Tr2 DT but that all four are required to induce Chk1 expression.
evidence: Inferred from differential effects of single ligand knockdowns on Fz3 vs Chk1 expression.

claim: Tracheoblasts that enter mitosis prematurely in L3 in Wnt/Chk1-deficient backgrounds continue to divide post mitotic re-entry.
source: The subsequent timecourse of cell proliferation in these mutants reveals that tracheoblasts that enter mitosis prematurely in L3 continue to divide post mitotic re-entry (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by cell count data over time shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Dpp signaling is required for proliferation of tracheoblasts post mitotic re-entry.
source: A previous study has identified Dpp (the Drosophila homolog of TGF-β) as the signal required for proliferation of tracheoblasts post mitotic re-entry.
evidence: Referenced from previous study (Djabrayan and Casanova, 2016).

claim: Dpp signaling (pMad immunostaining) was undetectable in cells in G2 arrest and observed mid L3 onwards once the cells start dividing.
source: Pertinently, an earlier study on tracheoblasts showed that Dpp signaling (pMad immunostaining) was undetectable in cells in G2 arrest and observed mid L3 onwards once the cells start dividing (Djabrayan and Casanova, 2016).
evidence: Referenced from previous study and confirmed by data in Figure 5A.

claim: pMad immunostaining was undetectable in L2 and early L3 (0–8 h L3 and 16–24 h L3) and nuclear localized at 32–40 h L3, once the cells entered mitosis.
source: As reported previously, pMad immunostaining was undetectable in L2 and early L3 (0–8 h L3 and 16–24 h L3) and nuclear localized at 32–40 h L3, once the cells entered mitosis (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by pMad immunostaining data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Abundant nuclear localized pMad signal was detected in Btl-Chk1RNAi and Btl-Wnt6RNAi at 16–24 h L3.
source: We stained Btl-Chk1RNAi and Btl-Wnt6RNAi at 16–24 h L3 for pMad and detected abundant nuclear localized signal (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by pMad immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Release from G2 arrest leads to the concomitant upregulation of Dpp signaling that further stimulates proliferation.
source: This suggested that release from G2 arrest leads to the concomitant upregulation of Dpp signaling that further stimulates proliferation.
evidence: Inferred from pMad staining in Chk1 and Wnt mutants showing premature Dpp activation.

claim: pMad immunostaining was undetectable in Btl-TkvQD animals at L2.
source: We found that pMad immunostaining was undetectable in Btl-TkvQD animals at L2 (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by pMad immunostaining data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Arrest in G2 prevents the activation of Dpp signaling and exit from G2 leads to the activation of Dpp signaling and continued cell proliferation.
source: Taken together, these observations suggest that arrest in G2 prevents the activation of Dpp signaling and that exit from G2 leads to the activation of Dpp signaling and continued cell proliferation.
evidence: Inferred from pMad staining patterns in arrested vs dividing cells and in mutants.

claim: Arrested tracheoblasts, and the tracheae they comprise, grow significantly during the period in which the cells are arrested in G2.
source: We have previously reported that arrested tracheoblasts, and the tracheae they comprise, grow significantly during the period in which the cells are arrested in G2.
evidence: Referenced from previous study (Kizhedathu et al., 2018).

claim: Premature exit from arrest resulting from the knockdown of Chk1 retards growth and results in a reduction in the overall size of Tr2 DT.
source: Premature exit from arrest resulting from the knockdown of Chk1 retards growth and results in a reduction in the overall size of Tr2 DT (Figure 6A, Kizhedathu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by size measurement data shown in Figure 6A and previous publication.

claim: Compared to 268 ± 32% growth in length and 247 ± 19% growth in width in control animals, TCF mutants grew only by 178 ± 8% in length and 176 ± 13% in width between L2 and 32–40 h L3.
source: Quantification of percentage growth between L2 and 32–40 h L3 revealed that compared to a 268 ± 32% (n = 6 tracheae) growth in length and 247 ± 19% (n = 12 tracheae) growth in width in control animals (Kizhedathu et al., 2018), TCF mutants grew only by 178 ± 8% (n = 6 tracheae) in length and 176 ± 13% (n = 6 tracheae) in width.
evidence: Supported by quantitative measurements of tracheal size.

claim: Wnt signaling is required for growth of the thoracic tracheae during larval stages.
source: Thus, consistent with our earlier finding that Chk1 is required for optimal tracheal growth, Wnt signaling is also required for growth of the thoracic tracheae during larval stages.
evidence: Inferred from growth measurements in TCF mutants compared to controls.

claim: Tracheoblasts express both drivers of G2-M (Cdc2/Cdk1, CyclinB, Stg) and simultaneously activate negative regulators of G2-M (Chk1).
source: An unusual aspect of G2 arrest in Tr2 DT is that the cells express both drivers of G2-M (Cdc2/Cdk1, CyclinB, Stg) and simultaneously activate negative regulators of G2-M (Chk1, [Kizhedathu et al., 2018], this study).
evidence: Stated as observation from this study and previous work.

claim: The loss of Stg, Cdc2/Cdk1, or Cyclin B led to a reduction in the size of Tr2 DT at 32–40 h L3.
source: The loss of any one of these G2-M drivers led to a reduction in the size of Tr2 DT (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by size measurement data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The juxtaposition of positive and negative regulators is required for the growth of the tracheoblasts and the tracheae they comprise.
source: These data suggest that the juxtaposition of positive and negative regulators is required for the growth of the tracheoblasts and the tracheae they comprise (see model in Figure 6B).
evidence: Inferred from data showing both positive and negative regulators are needed for optimal growth.

claim: Progenitors of the thoracic tracheal system of adult Drosophila arrest in G2 in a Chk1-dependent manner during larval stages.
source: Progenitors of the thoracic tracheal system of adult Drosophila arrest in G2 in a Chk1-dependent manner during larval stages.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a summary of findings.

claim: Chk1 is transcriptionally upregulated in arrested tracheoblasts by the canonical Wnt signaling pathway and this upregulation is sufficient to induce arrest.
source: We find that Chk1 is transcriptionally upregulated in arrested tracheoblasts by the canonical Wnt signaling pathway and that this upregulation is sufficient to induce arrest.
evidence: Supported by qPCR, reporter, and rescue experiment data.

claim: Wnt signaling is activated by four Wnt ligands - Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6, Wnt10 – that are all expressed in the tracheoblasts.
source: Our studies reveal that Wnt signaling is activated by four Wnt ligands - Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6, Wnt10 – that are all expressed in the tracheoblasts.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and smFISH data showing expression of these ligands.

claim: All four Wnt ligands (Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6, Wnt10) are required for Chk1 upregulation.
source: We show that all four ligands are required for Chk1 upregulation and that the temporal expression of the ligands is also under transcriptional control.
evidence: Supported by data showing each ligand knockdown reduces Chk1 expression.

claim: Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6, and Wnt10 are high when the cells are arrested in G2 and low at the time the cells enter division.
source: Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6, and Wnt10 are high when the cells are arrested in G2 and low at the time the cells enter division.
evidence: Supported by qPCR and smFISH data showing temporal expression patterns.

claim: The ligands (Wg, Wnt5, Wnt6, Wnt10) act synergistically to maintain a threshold of Wnt signaling necessary for Chk1 expression.
source: We hypothesize that the ligands act synergistically to maintain a threshold of Wnt signaling necessary for Chk1 expression.
evidence: Hypothesized based on data showing all ligands are required and none are dispensable.

claim: Overexpression of Wnt5 or Wnt10 in Wnt6RNAi-expressing animals was able to prevent precocious proliferation at 16–24 h L3.
source: Consistent with this, we found that overexpression of Wnt5 or Wnt10 in Wnt6RNAi-expressing animals was able to prevent precocious proliferation at 16–24 h L3 (Btl-Wnt6RNAi at 16–24 h L3 Avg: 32.4 ± 1.2 cells, n = 8 tracheae; Btl-Wnt6RNAi, Wnt5 at 16–24 h L3 Avg: 19.1 ± 0.8, n = 8 tracheae; Btl-Wnt6RNAi, Wnt10 at 16–24 h L3 Avg: 18.2 ± 1.7 cells, n = 8 tracheae).
evidence: Supported by cell count data in rescue experiments.

claim: Wnt5 facilitates canonical Wnt signaling in tracheoblasts.
source: It is noteworthy that Wnt5, which in Drosophila has been implicated in non-canonical Wnt signaling (Shimizu et al., 2011), facilitates canonical Wnt signaling in tracheoblasts.
evidence: Inferred from data showing Wnt5 is required for canonical Wnt target expression and G2 arrest.

claim: Non-canonical Wnt ligands can activate canonical Wnt signaling in some systems.
source: There is evidence in other systems that non-canonical Wnt ligands can activate canonical Wnt signaling (Fu et al., 2016; Lyons et al., 2004).
evidence: Cited from published studies.

claim: Both Derailed and Doughnut, RYK family receptors that mediate non-canonical Wnt signaling, are expressed in the larval tracheal system.
source: Preliminary expression profiling of the larval tracheal system has indicated that both Derailed and Doughnut, RYK family receptors that mediate non-canonical Wnt signaling, are expressed (AG, AK unpublished).
evidence: Stated as unpublished observation from expression profiling.

claim: Wnt5 could act either directly or indirectly to facilitate canonical Wnt signaling in tracheoblasts.
source: This suggests that Wnt5 could act either directly or indirectly to facilitate canonical Wnt signaling in tracheoblasts.
evidence: Speculated based on expression of non-canonical receptors.

claim: Radioresistant tumor cells exhibit higher levels of Wnt signaling that leads to upregulation of Myc expression and in turn Chk1/2 expression.
source: Radioresistant tumor cells exhibit higher levels of Wnt signaling that leads to upregulation of Myc expression and in turn Chk1/2 expression (Zhao et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from published study.

claim: Wnt-dependent upregulation of Chk1 could be a general mechanism for the activation of a G2 checkpoint.
source: It is plausible that Wnt-dependent upregulation of Chk1 evidenced here and in other contexts could be a general mechanism for the activation of a G2 checkpoint.
evidence: Speculated based on findings in this study and in tumor cells.

claim: Tr2 tracheoblasts switch from hypertrophic growth to hyperplastic growth during larval life.
source: Tr2 tracheoblasts switch from hypertrophic growth to hyperplastic growth during larval life.
evidence: Stated as observation about growth mode transitions.

claim: The balance between hypertrophic and hyperplastic growth modes determines tracheal size at the onset of pupariation.
source: The balance between these modes of growth determines tracheal size at the onset of pupariation.
evidence: Inferred from growth measurements in mutants affecting the timing of the switch.

claim: Withdrawal of negative regulators like Wnt/Chk1 leads to a precocious switch from hypertrophy to hyperplasty and to a reduction in tracheal size.
source: We have shown that withdrawal of negative regulators like Wnt/Chk1 leads to a precocious switch from hypertrophy to hyperplasty and to a reduction in tracheal size.
evidence: Supported by size measurements in Wnt and Chk1 mutants.

claim: The withdrawal of either positive or negative cell cycle regulators perturbs growth of tracheoblasts.
source: We show here that the juxtaposition of positive and negative regulators is essential for hypertrophic growth and that the withdrawal of either positive or negative regulators perturbs growth.
evidence: Supported by size measurements showing reduced growth in both Chk1 mutants and G2-M driver mutants.

claim: The findings about growth control in tracheoblasts could be broadly relevant to growth control in other systems.
source: These findings could be broadly relevant to growth control in other systems.
evidence: Speculated based on the general principle observed.

claim: Tracheoblasts increase approximately 11 fold in volume while arrested in G2.
source: The tracheoblasts, and the tracheae they comprise, grow in size while arrested (increase ~11 fold in volume) and undergo rapid size-reductive divisions thereafter (cell division time ~10 hr)(Kizhedathu et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from previous publication.

claim: Tracheoblasts undergo rapid size-reductive divisions with a cell division time of approximately 10 hr after exiting G2 arrest.
source: The tracheoblasts, and the tracheae they comprise, grow in size while arrested (increase ~11 fold in volume) and undergo rapid size-reductive divisions thereafter (cell division time ~10 hr)(Kizhedathu et al., 2018).
evidence: Cited from previous publication.

claim: Loss of ATR/Chk1 results in tracheoblasts initiating mitoses precociously.
source: Loss of ATR/Chk1 results in tracheoblasts initiating mitoses precociously.
evidence: Cited from previous publication and confirmed in this study.

claim: There was no evidence for DNA damage in arrested tracheoblasts.
source: Although the activation of ATR/Chk1 has typically been associated with DNA damage, there was no evidence for DNA damage in arrested tracheoblasts.
evidence: Stated as observation from previous work.

claim: A pulse of Drosophila steroid hormone Ecdysone induces the expression of Cdc25/Stg mRNA in imaginal histoblasts.
source: For example, a pulse of Drosophila steroid hormone Ecdysone has been shown to induce the expression of Cdc25/Stg mRNA in imaginal histoblasts (Ninov et al., 2009).
evidence: Cited from published study.

claim: The Notch and Wnt signaling pathways repress the expression of Stg in neural precursors in the wing imaginal disc.
source: Along these lines, the Notch and Wnt signaling pathways repress the expression of Stg in neural precursors in the wing imaginal disc (Johnston and Edgar, 1998).
evidence: Cited from published study.

claim: Insulin signaling upregulates Stg protein levels via repression of Tribbles expression in neural stem cells.
